note: What was assessed and why, for the zkvm/host RustSec findings of designation mldsa65-withdrawal-d1. Not a security waiver and not a fix: every finding below is still present in zkvm/host/Cargo.lock. Derived by scripts/generate-sp1-host-advisories.ts from the observation, the claims in scripts/lib/sp1-host-advisories.ts and the repository; never hand-edit it. See docs/SP1_Host_Lockfile_Advisories.md.

ownerDecision.scope: zkvm/host/Cargo.lock under designation mldsa65-withdrawal-d1: no host dependency is updated and d1 is kept; the compatible dependency refresh waits for the next actual program rebuild
ownerDecision.source: owner decision after the read-only zkvm/host RustSec assessment of 2026-10-16 (after PR #219): defer the host lockfile updates to the next program rebuild and keep d1 and the lockfile as they are

assessment.yankedSource: https://index.crates.io/ (cargo audit ran with --no-yanked; an index that does not answer fails the measurement)
assessment.dependencyStatusMeaning: derived from the measured findings alone: NOT_DEPENDENCY_SAFE while any RustSec vulnerability or unsoundness is locked in zkvm/host/Cargo.lock, whatever its bucket. A valid assessment records what was assessed and why; it does not make a vulnerable dependency non-vulnerable.

advisory.title: Invalid pointer dereference in `fmt::Pointer` impl for `Atomic` and `Shared` when the underlying pointer is invalid

findings.precondition: formatting an Atomic or Shared that holds an invalid (e.g. null) pointer with its pointer formatting
findings.exploit: an invalid pointer dereference (undefined behaviour) inside the formatting impl
findings.rationale: crossbeam-epoch is linked through rayon's work-stealing deques, and no crate that can name its types formats one as a pointer

advisory.title: h2 unbounded empty DATA frames

findings.precondition: an HTTP/2 connection to a peer that sends empty DATA frames faster than the stream is drained
findings.exploit: unbounded memory growth, or a panic on length overflow (denial of service)
findings.rationale: h2 is linked through hyper (for reqwest and tonic), but no HTTP/2 connection is ever made: reqwest is built without http2 (HTTP/1.1 only), and no tonic transport is ever constructed, since sp1-prover uses tonic only for error types and sp1-sdk's gRPC client lives in its network module, which is not compiled

advisory.title: Remote memory exhaustion in quinn-proto from unbounded out-of-order stream reassembly

findings.precondition: a QUIC connection (quinn) to a malicious peer
findings.exploit: memory exhaustion from unbounded out-of-order stream reassembly (remote peer)
findings.rationale: cargo tree prints nothing for quinn-proto on any target: it is in Cargo.lock only because reqwest's rustls feature names quinn?/ring (a weak dependency feature), while reqwest's http3 feature, the only one that enables quinn, is off

advisory.title: TLS 1.3 handshake messages incorrectly accepted across encryption level boundaries

findings.precondition: a TLS 1.3 server that sends handshake messages across a key change in one record
findings.exploit: rustls accepts such messages instead of aborting; the transcript stays authenticated, so the peer cannot alter or complete a handshake (low impact)
findings.rationale: rustls is compiled, and its one use is the HTTPS download of SP1's circuit artifacts; nothing else in the host opens a TLS connection
findings.condition: rustls runs only inside SP1's own circuit download: release-mode install_circuit_artifacts at the Groth16/PLONK wrap stage, when the v6.1.0 circuit directory is absent (dev mode downloads with the aws CLI instead). The frozen proving configuration installs the circuit from a hash-verified WalletWall archive first, so that download never runs; until the archive path exists no proving run is authorized at all

advisory.title: `Debug` impls for client session values expose TLS secrets

findings.precondition: a custom ClientSessionStore that formats stored session values with Debug (for example into logs)
findings.exploit: disclosure of a TLS 1.2 master secret or TLS 1.3 resumption PSK to readers of those logs
findings.rationale: no crate that configures rustls here installs a session store of its own, and rustls's built-in cache redacts its Debug output

advisory.title: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to 1 GiB before authentication

findings.precondition: rustls's non-default brotli feature, connecting to a malicious server
findings.exploit: a five-byte header makes certificate decompression allocate up to 1 GiB before authentication (denial of service)
findings.rationale: rustls is built without brotli, and no brotli crate is in the lockfile

advisory.title: Unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange

findings.precondition: a client that offers a hybrid post-quantum key-exchange group (X25519MLKEM768) and keeps sessions across connections to one server
findings.exploit: an unauthenticated ServerHello pins later handshakes to classical X25519 (loss of post-quantum confidentiality; no authentication bypass)
findings.rationale: the only rustls provider compiled here is ring, whose groups are X25519, P-256 and P-384: there is no hybrid group to downgrade from

advisory.title: Decompression bomb in `ruzstd`: a tiny input can exhaust memory (OOM)

findings.exploit: a crafted .zst under 128 KB allocates gigabytes (out-of-memory denial of service)
findings.rationale: ruzstd is compiled because sp1-core-executor enables object's default compression feature, but its decoder is reached only through object's section decompression, which no crate here calls: sp1-core-executor only writes ELF dumps, and backtrace decompresses debug sections itself, with its zstd path behind its own ruzstd feature, which is off

advisory.title: `IterMut` violates Stacked Borrows by invalidating internal pointer

findings.exploit: a Stacked Borrows violation in IterMut (undefined behaviour for code that iterates mutably)
findings.rationale: sp1-prover, lru's only dependent, keeps two caches and never calls iter_mut

advisory.title: Potential use-after-free due to lack of panic safety in `LruCache::pop()`

findings.precondition: LruCache::pop with a key whose Drop panics, the panic caught by catch_unwind
findings.exploit: a use-after-free or double free on a later eviction (memory corruption)
findings.rationale: sp1-prover never calls pop on its caches, never catches an unwind, and its cache keys have no Drop impl

advisory.title: Unchecked pointer offset in crate `memmap2`

findings.precondition: calling advise_range, unchecked_advise_range, flush_range or flush_async_range with an out-of-bounds range
findings.exploit: an invalid pointer offset passed to madvise or msync (undefined behaviour; the pointer is not dereferenced)
findings.rationale: no dependent of memmap2 calls any of the affected functions

reassessWhen: zkvm/host's tree changes at HEAD or on disk (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, build.rs or src/main.rs), including a dependabot bump
a designation succeeds mldsa65-withdrawal-d1, or d1's bytes change (designations are immutable: supersede, never rewrite)

an assumption stops holding: a new dependency, table or sp1-sdk feature (network, cuda, native-gnark), a network-only, aws-lc, brotli or cuda crate in the lockfile, another proof kind or prover in src/main.rs
proving availability changes: a WalletWall circuit archive, a local copy, an exercised self-hosted path (the archive-only install changes which rustls path can run)
the networked RustSec job reports drift: a new advisory, a changed one (kind, severity, ranges), a finding that disappeared, or a changed graph, feature, source or fix fact
the measurement script, the evidence catalog or the claims change
nextProgramRebuild: apply the compatible dependency refresh listed under remediation.compatibleRefresh (and any newer patched releases)
re-audit every lockfile and re-measure this record's observation with the pinned cargo-audit

publish a successor designation for the rebuilt program (a host-only change is refused as a same-identity successor: the rebuild itself must change the program's identity, or the owner decides the designation route)
run the canonical two-host rebuild and record its procedure
re-measure the ELF and PROGRAM_VKEY outside the build and compare them
re-measure proving availability for the new lockfile and circuit
